A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Type-R study, with readable main text and Appendices A-K. Equations, pseudocode, tables, figures, and supplementary material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original MARIO-Eval experiments, human ratings, ablations, and supplementary analyses, including results in Tables 1-12.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark results, human-study outcomes, ablations, and supplementary analyses in Tables 1-12.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same error detection and matching, text erasing, layout regeneration, and iterative typo correction pipeline, with the same components.

E1.justification: MARIO-Eval evaluation, MARIO-LAION validation, and the existing long-prompt, layout, and word-count scenarios are retained. No datasets, tasks, or evaluation populations are added or removed.

E2.justification: The TextDiffuser models, naive rendering baselines, and OCR, eraser, and text-editor comparators remain unchanged, including the appendix comparisons. Reference renumbering does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain the 5,414-prompt main evaluation, 500-prompt analysis subset, separate 500-prompt validation set, metrics, and correction settings. The 100-prompt, five-participant human study is also unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.6-4.7 and Appendices A-J retain the same pipeline and backend ablations, iteration analysis, filtering grid search, error counts, GPT-human comparisons, capacity analysis, and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains its ± reporting, Section 4.5 retains the paired t-tests, and Appendix A retains averaging over five GPT and human ratings. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1-12 retain their numerical results; for example, Table 1's Type-R with Flux remains at 7.67 for graphic design and 62.0 for OCR. Plotted results and qualitative examples are retained; Figure 15 reorders existing panels.

T1.justification: The optimal transport formulation and definitions for padded word sets in Equations (1)-(3) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of automatic typo correction without fine-tuning, compatibility with different image generators, and improved text accuracy while preserving design quality.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 now attributes TextDiffuser-2's corruption on long prompts to CLIP's inability to process tokens beyond 77. This adds a specific explanation for an existing result; the broader limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1's page 2 footnote promises a future open-source implementation. v2's page 1 footnote announces availability and provides code and project-page links. Implementation settings and Appendix K's prompt templates otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Zhao et al.'s Harmonizing Visual Text Comprehension and Generation, while the OpenCOLE bibliography entry is removed. The broader research positioning is unchanged; other reference edits mainly concern numbering and metadata.

P1.justification: v2 corrects Seiichi Uchida's name, adds Japan to the affiliation, makes limited prose edits, and reformats references. Section organization remains intact. Appendix B introduces an unresolved citation displayed as [15?].

P2.justification: Figure 5 changes marker symbols and its legend, Figure 6 adjusts panel alignment, and Figure 15 swaps the intermediate and final panels for the Advantage Driver Training example. Footnote and reference layout also shift locally; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Replacing the release promise with code/project links and correcting Figure 15's panel placement modestly improve usability and interpretability. The long-prompt explanation adds useful context. These limited gains outweigh the small regression from Appendix B's unresolved citation; the scientific method and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
